svg.aria-label: One onychomycosis example: keep the evidence, remove one relation
svg.text: One onychomycosis example: keep the evidence, remove one relation
The student eventually answers correctly; the existing station rule also requires a prompt-dependent C+ ceiling.

g.text: 1 · Same input and cached extraction
Student omits interaction → authorised doctor prompt is delivered → student explains the interaction.
Save the system’s own Evidence Graph once. Do not repair it using the faculty reference.
Keep dialogue, student evidence, clinical knowledge and Rule Graph unchanged.
2 · FULL: retain the intervention relation
The prompt event is linked to the assessed requirement.
The same graph engine sees the student’s answer
and the fact that it followed the actual prompt.
2 · UNLINKED: block only this relation
The prompt event remains in the original log.
Its assessment-consequence relation is filtered.
Student evidence and all other relations remain.
3 · Expected mechanism behaviour
Criterion completion can be recognised.
The linked prompt-dependent cap can be executed.
C+ is a ceiling, not an automatic final grade.
3 · What the experiment checks
Criterion completion can still be recognised.
Does blocking the relation omit the required cap?
Record no effect, extraction errors and failures.
4 · Compare both actual outputs with one independent reference
A change alone is not a success. The correct outcome must follow the original approved checklist.
Verify identical evidence/rule hashes, the filtered edge IDs and unchanged non-target processing.
5 · Negative controls must remain unchanged
Unsent draft · independent answer · ordinary patient confirmation · station without this cap
Do not copy the C1 consequence to diuretics. Correction and source attribution must remain intact.

svg.text: Mechanism illustration, not measured performance. Role generation is not rerun in this ablation.
